messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a 503 spike (P95 requests) from hosted inference around 11:42 UTC. Customer: bluebox. Symptoms: rapid upstream worker exits in nvlink-prod-3 pool.

kyle: yup, logs show repeated GPU driver resets then SIGSEGV in upstream runner. snippet:
```
[2024-11-02T11:42:12Z] runner[pid=2145] ERROR: cuda: nvlink_pipe_write failed: -74
[2024-11-02T11:42:12Z] runner[pid=2145] SIGSEGV at 0x7f...
```

oncall: routing rule applied to drain nvlink-prod-3 -> fallback to cpu-pool-2, @deploy-bot triggered failover :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: traffic re-route to fallback pools started (id=rout-20241102-1143).

cs: pinging support, telling customer we're executing mitigation and will follow up in 15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

dan: quick analysis — driver reset appears correlated with high concurrent small-batch requests plus nvlink pipe saturation. seen a fork+pipe error in kernel logs:
```
Nov  2 11:42:11 host kernel: nvlink0: pipe 3: broken; fork() returned -EPIPE
```

kyle: repro (local infra): run embed-sparce-load with model mm-large, ctx 8192, concurrency 120, nvlink pipelining enabled -> observe reset within 3-5 minutes. I added exact command to the thread.

maria: mitigation steps taken: 1) disable nvlink pipelining on nvlink-prod-3 2) reduce max_concurrency to 60 3) enable circuit-breaker to reject >75 req/s from same API key. applied at 11:46 UTC.

oncall: metrics look better at 11:51 — error rate down to baseline. still watching p95. rolling back one config that increased kernel launch parallelism earlier today.

cs: updated ticket #9876: "Mitigation applied, monitoring. No additional customer impact reported." sending NRR timeline.

kyle: next actions: collect full kernel oops/kmsg, get nv driver version and file a driver-bisect if needed. add E2E test for small-batch high-concurrency on nvlink pools.

maria: allocating followups: ENG-1152 collect crash artifacts, ENG-1153 test coverage, ENG-1154 playbook entry. tagging @oncall for postmortem notes.

oncall: thanks all — lowering priority after stabilization but keeping incident open until artifacts collected. :eyes:
